Mouse or keyboard: arrows and Tab move, Enter or Space confirms, Escape steps back. In battle: 1–9 pick an action, Tab cycles targets, S cycles speed, A toggles auto-battle, click or Space skips an animation.
{action}: pick a target. Right-click or Escape to go back.
{action}: pick a tile. Right-click or Escape to go back.
Hover or focus a card to see its details.
afraid: can only Defend or Move away from the front
{event} waits: it can be resumed later.
The party makes camp and rests.
The party rests at the Sanctuary.
Everyone has collapsed: the party makes camp.
Everyone has collapsed: the party rests at the Sanctuary.

A wooden cage sits crooked beside the trail. Goblin carpentry runs mostly on enthusiasm. Inside, a merchant flings himself at the bars. "Goblins! They took my wife! My boy! My cart, which I had only just finished paying for! Their Gatekeeper has the key!"
Tear the bars apart. It will not be quiet.
Pick the lock. The pick looks nervous.
Leave him for now. He'll keep.
The merchant is still in his cage, and still shouting. "You came back! I knew it! I had already composed my last words. They were mostly about the cart."
Tear the bars apart. It will not be quiet.
Pick the lock. The pick looks nervous.
Leave him again. He'll manage, loudly.
{hero} grabs the bars and heaves. The cage, never fully committed to being a cage, comes apart with an almighty crack. Nearby, two goblin voices shout and come running.
The lock snaps, and the pick with it. Two goblin guards burst from the brush, blades drawn and dinner plans forming.
{hero} works the lock in silence. A soft click, and the door swings open. The merchant nearly faints with relief.
The Gatekeeper's key turns in the lock. It is the only part of the cage that works properly.

The merchant presses a few coins into {hero}'s hand, then, after a visible struggle, one more. "Bartleby Crumpwhistle, forever in your debt! They went east, past the Gatekeeper's post. Find my family! I'll wait at the trail. And find the cart, if it's no trouble!"
The trail sinks into black, still water, and the only way on is through it. A sign on a dead tree reads NO SWIMMING. Someone has underlined it twice. Something has bitten off the corner.
Wade across, watching the water. After all, wading isn't swimming!
{hero} spots a log drifting toward the party, against the current. Logs do not do that. Logs also do not have teeth! The crocodile lunges into a party that is ready for it.
The water explodes! A crocodile the length of a rowboat surges out of the murk, all teeth and no manners, and lunges for the nearest hero.
Inside the crocodile, the party finds a pouch of coins, an unbroken potion, and most of the rest of the sign.

A shallow cave, ringed with carefully piled bones picked very clean. Skulls line the entrance in a row, the way other households keep flowerpots. Peeking inside, you can faintly see some neatly sorted scraps of meat. Snarls echo from deeper within. Several wolves, by the sound of it, all hungry.
Scare the pack off. Be the scariest thing here.
Go in and explore. The wolves will most likely object.
Walk away. Let the wolves keep their flowerpots.
{hero} bellows into the cave and bangs steel on stone. A long, thoughtful silence follows. Then the whole pack bolts for the trees, leaving their scraps behind, still neatly sorted!
The pack lies still. Among the tidy rows of bones, the party finds a dead traveler's coins and a potion, filed neatly with the rest.

A mossy altar sits in a clearing, its vines woven through it so neatly it looks deliberate. A name is carved on top. Time has worn it down to a Y and a hopeful smudge. Someone still leaves offerings here. Nobody remembers why.
Read the carvings and perform the rite. Properly.
Pray anyway. Surely it's the thought that counts?
Leave it be. Let the smudge rest.
{hero} traces the carvings and performs the rite: three bows, one turn, and a respectful nod to the smudge. The vines loosen slightly, which seems like approval.

A warm wind stirs the clearing, and the forest snaps into focus. For a moment the whole world looks carefully stitched together, apart from a few bits nobody quite finished. The party's eyes stay sharp for a while.
The vines tighten. The moss darkens, and the air goes cold. Whatever lives here did not care for that prayer! The party's arms feel heavy, as if something has tied a knot in every muscle.

A deep mud pit swallows the trail. Here and there, lone boots stand upright in the muck, left by travelers who decided they valued their feet more. The mud gurgles contentedly, clearly hoping for a matching pair.
March straight through. Mud respects a firm stride.
Look for something to step on.
Go the long way around. Slow, but the boots stay dry.
{hero} sets a pace the mud simply cannot argue with. The party marches through without breaking stride, and every boot comes out the far side still attached.
{hero} notes that the tops of the boots are dry, and hops from one to the next like stepping stones! The party follows, leaving the mud hungry.
Waist-deep, one sucking step at a time. The mud does its very best to keep a boot. It fails! But the party comes out the far side exhausted.
The detour winds through thorns and bramble for hours. Behind the party, the mud gurgles in disappointment. Everyone's legs stay heavy for a while.

A ransacked camp: torn tents, a cold fire pit, and supplies scattered in the dirt. Goblin work, judging by the bite marks on the cooking pot. One bedroll has a name stitched into it: BARTLEBY CRUMPWHISTLE. Beside it lies a receipt for one cart, paid in full.
Search carefully. There's always a catch!
{hero} spots a snare hidden under a bedroll and springs it with a stick. The stick loses. Somewhere, a goblin's tummy growls.
A snare hidden under a bedroll snaps shut on an unlucky ankle! Goblin snares are crude and rusty, but they mean every bit of it.
There's enough here to pack up and carry for a camp later. Or the crates could feed the fire pit and make this a safe place to rest. The crates are the only dry wood, so it's one or the other.
Pack the supplies for a camp later. Waste not!
Burn the crates. A safe place to rest, right here.
Under a tent, the party finds a few coins and a potion the goblins missed. They were busy with the cooking pot.

A guard post blocks the only path east: a palisade with one sturdy gate. Before it stand three goblins. The middle one wears a helmet meant for a warrior twice his size. "HALT!" he proclaims. "None pass the Gatekeeper!" He jangles a large iron key. "Also, the Gatekeeper is me."
Point behind them and shout: "Look! A distraction!"
Frighten off his guards. Some goblins scare easily.
Charge into battle. That helmet won't save him.
Promise to return. Gatekeepers never leave the gate.
Every goblin turns to look, the Gatekeeper included. By the time they turn back, the party is upon them!

{hero} stands tall, weapon raised, with a look that asks which of them plans to fall with the gate. One guard drops his spear and flees into the trees. The other stays, visibly shaken. So, a little, does the Gatekeeper.

The Gatekeeper sinks to his knees. "Tell them... the Gatekeeper... kept the gate..." *Clonk*. His helmet keeps rolling long after he stops. The iron key drops into the dirt, the gate creaks open behind him, and the path east lies clear.
A woman's scream cuts through the trees. "Help! Help! They're gonna turn me into stew!" She appears to be tied to a tree, alone, with suspiciously bushy bushes all around.
Rush to free her before she's stew!
{hero} points out that one of the bushes has ears. The bush, offended, draws a knife. Goblin raiders pour out, but the party is ready for them!
The bushes explode with goblins! Not literally.

"Thank you, heroes!" the woman cries as the party frees her. "But they still have my son! Please, I don't want my boy to be goblin stew!" She brightens at news of her husband, then narrows her eyes. "Did he ask about the cart?" She presses her last potions into the party's hands. "The fortress is east. Bring my Tobble home!"

"Thank you, heroes!" the woman cries as the party frees her. "But they still have my son! Please, I don't want my boy to be goblin stew!" Her husband, she explains, is caged near the forest edge, probably still shouting about the cart. "Their fortress is east. Please, bring my Tobble home."
The path narrows between two steep banks. It's quiet. Too quiet. The birds must have all gone to sing somewhere else?
Birds know things. Watch the ground as you proceed.
{hero} stops the party just short of a wire stretched across the path. It runs up the bank to a stack of spiked logs, held back by a knot no self-respecting sailor would tie.
Disarm it and keep the spikes. Goblins won't miss them.
Step over it. High knees, everyone!
One by one, the party high-steps over the wire like a very dignified parade. The logs stay where they are, sulking.
{hero} unpicks the goblin knot, amazed it even held anything, then pries the iron spikes out of the logs. These could come in handy.

{hero}'s leg catches the wire. *SPROING!* Spiked logs thunder down the bank and catch {hero} with a nasty, bleeding gash. Up the path, a goblin patrol cheers and comes jogging down to see what it caught.

A crude lookout platform rises above the trees, held together by rope, optimism, and one very tired ladder. Three goblin lookouts seem to be sleeping at the top. From up there, you could probably see the whole valley.
Climb up the ladder slowly and quietly.
Rush the tower quickly before the goblins can react.
Leave the lookouts to their nap.
{hero} climbs the ladder quiet as a snail, the goblins remaining fast asleep. The view is absolutely incredible!

The whole valley spreads out below: a boar rooting in the grove, figures moving in the marsh, and the goblin fortress to the east. Someone has carved an arrow into the railing pointing at it, labeled HOME. A purse sits on the boards, unattended.
A rope snare dangles over the path, crude but obvious. Inside you see a small pile of coins, a good bait for human prey!
Disable the snare, shouldn't be too hard
Try to grab the gold without triggering the trap
Leave the gold, you're not falling for it!
{hero} carefully traces the rope and finds the bent sapling meant to be used as the trigger. After jamming a stick to block the release, the snare is effectively disabled.
{hero} reaches in carefully, trying to get the gold without touching the snare rope. Miraculously, or due to a defective trap, the arm returns with gold in hand!
{hero} tries to reach the gold but the trap is sprung! By the time {hero} is freed, Goblin hunters are upon them!
An enraged boar paws the dirt of its feeding ground, tusks low. It isn't the Mega Boar, but it has clearly been taking lessons. It has the temper already. It's working on the size.
Brace for the charge. Here it comes!
{hero} plants their feet and doesn't budge an inch. The party forms up around them, and the boar thunders straight into a wall of steel.
The party braces, but the boar is faster than it looks, and angrier than it is fast! It slams into the line before anyone can strike first.
That night, the party roasts the boar over a small fire. It tastes of temper and acorns. A good meal does wonders.
A carved monolith hums with old warding magic, its runes glowing faintly blue. Actually, more like a turquoise.
Drink in its power. It has plenty to spare.
Hum along with the stone, attune to its power.
Just touch it and see what happens!
{hero} presses both hands to the stone. Its power floods in, bright and cold, and stays. The stone hums a little lower, slightly put out, as the whole party's Mana surges.
{hero} hums along with the stone until the two find the same note. Delighted to finally have company, it shares its power with the whole party.
The runes are a boundary marker and, in the margins, a map: a chapel to the northeast is still warded and safe to rest in. The carver also left a note complaining about his wages.
A gentle pulse runs up the party's arms, and their Mana stirs. The stone seems to approve of the direct approach.
Sometimes the instinct to touch things pays off. This time, it does not. The party feels its magic seep away for a while.

A hermit sorts herbs on a flat rock, surrounded by baskets of leaves, roots, and one very carefully guarded basket of mushrooms. "Field medicine! Potions! For a fee, I'll set up my kit." She sees where you're looking. "DON'T TOUCH THE MUSHROOMS."
Pay her fee. Medicine isn't cheap.
Come back later. Leave the mushrooms alone.
The hermit and {hero} talk for hours about medicines, mushrooms and close calls with Pumpler vines. "Always great to chat with a fellow Pharmacognosist. For you, I'll set up for free!"
She unpacks kettles, vials, and a small hand-painted sign: POTIONS. NOT MUSHROOMS. Her Alchemist Station is open for business.

From cover, the party studies the goblin fortress. Smoke rises from a great cookpot inside its walls, smelling strongly of Pumpler Vine. A very nice merchant's cart is parked by the gate, next to a group of guards. From within comes the crying of a child.
Look for a back way in
Observe the guards and wait for an opportunity
Leave your cover and charge the guards at the gate.
Withdraw and prepare. This fight deserves your best.
{hero} sneaks around the camp's walls. On the far side, a rotting board smelling strongly of goblin urine can easily be kicked through.

{hero} notes a blind spot in the guards' line of sight: a stand of trees by the gate that any real soldiers would have cut down long ago. Using the trees as cover, the party creeps close enough to take the guards by surprise.
The party charges the gate. The outer patrol rushes out to meet it, shouting war cries, threats, and in one case a very detailed recipe.
The patrol is down, and the way into the fortress lies open. The smell of Pumpler Vine grows stronger.

In the middle of the camp, the Goblin Chief, the fattest goblin anyone has ever seen, is lowering a small boy toward the bubbling pot. A shaman spins in circles beside it for luck. The Chief turns, outraged. "Who dares interrupt LUNCH?"
"You have not seen... the last... of my appetite..." *Gurgle*. *SPLOOSH*. The Goblin Chief topples into his own stew. Out from behind a barrel peeks a small, very relieved boy.

Tobble runs into his mother's arms, and at the forest trail his father is waiting. The Crumpwhistles are together again! They empty their savings into the party's hands. Bartleby hugs his wife, then his son, and then, for slightly longer, his recovered cart.

The party brings Tobble back to his father at the forest trail, along with the cart. Bartleby weeps with joy, mostly over Tobble. His wife is still missing, but he swears he'll find her, and pays the party what he can.

Marigolda holds her son tight and doesn't let go for a long time. Her husband is still caged somewhere, she says, and she'll fetch him next. After the cart is safely home. She pays the party what she can.

Tobble is safe, but his family is nowhere to be found. The party sets off with him toward the forest edge to look for them. He solemnly hands over the few coins in his pocket, then asks if anyone has seen a cart.
